Reading a stack trace without panic

A stack trace is a list of places the program was, most recent first. The first line you understand is usually the useful one.

Error: cannot read property 'id' of undefined
    at renderRow (table.js:41:18)
    at renderTable (table.js:22:5)
    at update (app.js:9:3)

Start at the top and walk down until the frames stop being library code.

Inline references such as renderRow and table.js:41 keep their exact spelling.

function renderRow(row) {
  return row.id; // row was undefined
}

The fix is not always where the error was thrown. It is often one frame up, where the bad value was passed in.

The sidebar carries navigation and advertising, which should never be translated as content.
